known_risks: the Nigerian decider was trained on Nigerian facilities, mostly primary care
hospitals have many trust sites on one campus with similar names; one-to-one keeps the engine's top-scored site, which may be a ward block rather than the hospital's own code
ets includes non-hospital sites (clinics, offices); they stay in the population
no region has been looked at for hospitals; the twin count (598) and name/postcode agreement rates were seen when the source was found
question: On NHS hospitals (CQC acute NHS locations against ODS trust sites), does the adopted England workflow, engine + nigeria-facility-decider-v1 + one-to-one, find clearly more of the registries' twins than the engine without losing agreement?

rule.baseline: engine matches under the same one-to-one rule
rule.definition: user decision 2026-11-23: a unit or centre with its own site code on a hospital's grounds is a different facility from the hospital
rule.interpretation: pass: the England workflow covers NHS hospitals as well as GP practices. Recall gain below 5 points: the engine alone suffices for hospitals. Precision or twins-lost fail: report and do not extend the workflow to hospitals.
rule.lists: CQC HSCA active locations (2026-11-02), primary inspection category 'Acute hospital - NHS non-specialist' or '... specialist'; ODS ets, every site with no close date
rule.metrics: precision = kept links joining a CQC location to its twin / kept links whose CQC location has a twin in the region; recall = twins linked / every CQC hospital in the region whose twin is in the region (surfaced or not; X13 counted only surfaced ones); twins_lost = twins matched before one-to-one but not after
rule.pass: X13's bounds, pooled over all nine regions: precision >= engine precision - 0.001, recall >= engine recall + 0.05, twins_lost <= 0.1% of twins
rule.pipeline: engine matches stand; held pairs decided by the bundle as shipped; one-to-one: engine matches first by engine score, then decider matches by probability, ties by decision id; extra links become flags
rule.records: as X13: names upper-cased, region and local authority from postcode (ONSPD Aug 2026), CQC point else postcode centroid, ets postcode centroid; one engine run per English region
secondary: pair rule (X11 bounds) on labelled held pairs
flags by kind, flags on twins, pairs still held, decider rejects
rule.truth: CQC Location ID equals an ets site code in the same region (CQC uses ODS site codes as NHS location ids); this measures agreement with the registries' key
